plan: Model the check-in as a state machine over the public four-field `session` dict, with an action dispatch table in `handle` mapping the six action types to handler methods.

Apply validate-then-mutate guard clauses in every handler (state preconditions, payload type checks, known-id membership) so invalid actions return an error screen before any session mutation; a backstop try/except in `handle` enforces the never-raise rule.
Centralize prompt derivation in a next-unmet-prompt resolver (Confirm contact -> Choose appointment -> Review and complete) shared by corrections and error screens.

Build every screen through a single screen-factory that attaches appointment choices exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment` and otherwise emits an empty choices list; error screens prefix their first message with `Error:` and reuse the current-state prompt.

Use constructor-injected duck-typed ports (`action_source.read_action()`, `screen_sink.display(screen)`) so unittest fakes plug in with no framework; `run_once` raises RuntimeError before touching either port if one is missing, then reads, handles, displays once, and returns the same screen object.
Defensively copy the appointments sequence (dict-by-dict) at construction and rebuild choice dicts per screen so caller mutation cannot corrupt state.
mechanisms: Action dispatch table mapping action `type` strings to handler methods
Validate-then-mutate guard clauses with a shared active-and-incomplete precondition helper
Backstop exception handler in `handle` converting unexpected failures into `Error:` screens
Next-unmet-prompt resolver deriving the prompt from session state
Single screen-factory enforcing the choices-only-on-`Choose appointment` invariant
Constructor-injected I/O ports (action_source/screen_sink) enabling standard-library unittest fakes
Defensive copying of appointments and per-screen rebuilding of choice dicts
